lifecycle_rules.reply_obligation: Ordinary project messages may explicitly require a reply or a reply on completion. The daemon persists only the reply marker and timing requirement. Consumption and ACK never clear it; a correctly correlated reply from the current recipient to the original sender clears it atomically with the reply enqueue. The daemon does not infer business completion. Known idle with an outstanding marker emits one reminder per idle episode through the existing notification path; working and unknown do not. Reminders and replies default to no new reply requirement. Peer action results go to the requester; returning one result resumes the peer's own remaining work, and routine user reports are not required.
lifecycle_rules.work_specialties: Persist specialties by project and stable name. Project/category defaults, goal/category defaults and explicit task fields materialize one task policy. Roles are preferences; named executors and reviewers are requirements. Invitations, recipient acceptance, review acceptance, integration and cleanup remain separate facts. Changed delivery contracts invalidate old review acceptance; manual termination never proves delivery completion.
lifecycle_rules.loop: Every master goal, bug report/fix, master-to-subagent assignment, and peer task follows Trigger -> Work -> Gate -> State -> Stop.
lifecycle_rules.sequence: Declare board work and queue pending tasks -> claim or accept -> Verify -> Persist -> close applicable duties or record blocker -> inspect remaining work and blocker release -> continue eligible work or idle. Re-arm a consumed one-shot goal or deadline wake while scheduling remains necessary. Finite goal/task closure does not close the current master's standing project patrol; board-idle cancellation and periodic fallback follow skills/collab/references/board-idle-patrol.md.
lifecycle_rules.role_default: Default identity is peer. A new project master requires explicit user authorization, including a delegation routed by the current master. Existing legitimate roles recover through their current binding.
lifecycle_rules.wake: Master and ordinary peer each own their goal deadlines. Only master-idle requires current-master authority; legacy managed subworkers gain no independent scheduling authority. Board-idle patrol follows its canonical contract, including daemon-driven periodic fallback and owner-scoped task cancellation. A known-idle recipient with an explicit outstanding reply marker may receive one pending-reply reminder per idle episode; that reminder does not create a new task or schedule.
lifecycle_rules.worker_idle_fact: On each worker working -> idle transition, emit one idempotent worker-idle fact to the live master; this fact does not count or control the master idle reminder episode.
lifecycle_rules.master_idle_episode: Master idle reminders are level-triggered. Within the same master idle episode, each reminder attempt consumes the shared episode-local budget, up to three attempts. An observed working change ends that episode; after three consecutive attempts without an observed working change, the episode stops. Worker-idle facts do not count toward this budget, and there is no scheduling-turn counter or automatic rearm.
lifecycle_rules.name_ownership: A project-scoped stable name owns one current anchor and its work attribution; the current agent sessionID is the execution carrier. When current project/session/host facts uniquely continue the same name, update the current carrier and all unclosed board assignments without rewriting closed history. Source-name work does not follow a carrier that is authorized to take another name. A replaced holder receives no immediate companion name and may register an available name only on a later ordinary context.
lifecycle_rules.identity_lifecycle: Names are allocated from the ordinary pool and continue with peer-<number> when needed. A user-authorized restore or takeover replaces the target name's current holder. Automatic recovery requalifies only unique current session/block facts; historical files, archives, and old operation records cannot revive a replaced holder or veto explicit user authorization.
lifecycle_rules.identity_loss_return: Daemon-confirmed identity loss preserves the name and recovery path and starts one 15-minute same-name return window. A valid current holder return or same-name authorized replacement ends the wait. Repeated loss observations do not extend the same deadline. At expiry unresolved work becomes eligible for reassignment, but ownership changes only after the new owner accepts and the daemon commits. No legitimate idle recipient means the work remains assigned until valid capacity exists.
lifecycle_rules.explicit_retirement: Human retirement of an ordinary name releases that current name and makes unfinished work immediately eligible for reassignment; it does not wait for the 15-minute automatic-loss window. Work, message history, evidence, resources, and recovery references remain. Reassignment still requires legitimate idle capacity, invitation, and accepted/committed ownership. Automatic unknown, error, ask, offline, busy, or static silence is not retirement or idle.
lifecycle_rules.message_and_wake_handoff: On a committed same-name handoff, unconsumed messages and task wake targets follow the current holder and progress is preserved. Consumed message bodies, IDs, and true receipts remain historical and are not replayed. Late results are evaluated by the current task owner and do not restore the old holder.
lifecycle_rules.rex_activity: Rex observations keep presence and activity separate. working maps busy; blocked/question maps waiting_user; idle or done maps idle only when the current static evidence supports it; error maps error; missing or conflicting evidence maps unknown. Error, ask, unknown, busy, or static silence never counts as idle capacity.
lifecycle_rules.rex_session_naming: A project Rex session is named from the project cwd's final directory component. Peer identity, role, or task changes do not rename it. Rex binds the current server/session/block endpoint and does not require or infer tmux position 1; that fixed-position gate remains specific to tmux placement.
lifecycle_rules.sendmessage: Explicit collab sendmessage is immediate; idle, progress, delivery, bug, and worker-idle notices are auto-merged by the daemon in the 120-second batch window.
lifecycle_rules.bug_backlog: Bugs enter AppSDK or git-bug backlog with investigation evidence; P0 blocks the affected project.
lifecycle_rules.desktop: Goal ownership is independent of Desktop/TUI placement. Each master or peer registers and manages its own accepted long-horizon goal through the current public entrypoint.
lifecycle_rules.unknown_failure: Unknown occupancy, timeout and failure remain explicit. An unreachable or unknown endpoint does not delete the stable name or current anchor. Current explicit user recovery and takeover are not vetoed by unavailable historical arbitration. Pending, invitation, transport acceptance, and ACK do not prove ownership transfer or business completion. No fallback or fake success.
lifecycle_rules.review_gates: Use the current host orchestration review contract for independent Reviewer selection and milestone admission. This manifest defines no separate model/provider routing table.
lifecycle_rules.legacy: Legacy worker polling and managed production scheduling are not authoritative. Finite owner-goal schedules, current-master-only master-idle and daemon-driven board-idle patrol have distinct owners and lifecycles; use the canonical notification and board-idle references.
lifecycle_rules.verification_boundary: The source contract above records approved semantics and current source owners. Public black-box behavior, real frontend, loaded daemon, and integration evidence remain separate and pending where no receipt exists. This manifest does not turn declaration or file presence into behavior acceptance.

review_policy.milestone: independent milestone review under the current host orchestration contract

gate_descriptions.independent-review: Use an independent review path selected by the current host contract; do not duplicate host model routing here.
gate_descriptions.milestone-review: At the formal integration boundary, review the complete milestone after applicable author verification; Reviewer selection follows the current host contract.
gate_descriptions.loop-rules: Documented gate: each lifecycle is Trigger -> Work -> Gate -> State -> Stop and follows Discover -> durable dispatch intent -> Hand off -> Verify -> Persist -> Schedule.
gate_descriptions.bug-backlog: Documented gate: bugs are tracked in AppSDK/git-bug backlog and P0 blocks affected projects.
gate_descriptions.role-default: Documented gate: default identity is peer; master is explicit and user-approved.
gate_descriptions.worker-wake: Documented gate: each master or peer owns its goal deadline; only master-idle requires current-master authority. Board-idle uses the canonical patrol contract's fresh idle observation, periodic fallback and per-task owner cancellation. Busy and unknown do not receive board-idle input. Explicit reply markers and master-idle episode budgets remain separate from board-idle cycles; a completed goal does not close standing project patrol.
gate_descriptions.name-work-ownership: Name owns one current anchor and its work; agent sessionID is its execution carrier. Unique current facts continue unclosed assignments without rewriting closed history. Explicit user takeover is not vetoed by old history. Source-name work does not follow a carrier renamed to another name. The source declaration does not claim runtime verification.
gate_descriptions.identity-lifecycle: Declared gate: preserve one current anchor per allocated name, continue only on unique current facts, and never revive a replaced holder from history. The public context/query receipt is the observation path; runtime acceptance remains separately recorded.
gate_descriptions.identity-loss-return: Declared gate: daemon-confirmed identity loss starts one fixed 15-minute return window for automatic reassignment. Restart and repeated observations preserve its deadline. Managers can invite during the window. Ownership changes on invite acceptance plus daemon commit.
gate_descriptions.explicit-retirement: Declared gate: human retirement releases the exact current holder and starts immediate reassignment eligibility while preserving work, messages, resources, and recovery references. Ordinary names become available for registration. Retiring Jenny revokes that holder's precise master grant and retains Jenny as a master-only name. Eligibility persists while no legal master or idle target is available. Retirement, grant, board, invitation and acceptance receipts expose each result.
gate_descriptions.rex-activity: Declared gate: static error, question, unknown, busy, or missing evidence is not idle. Current Rex program status plus foreground owner is the source fact; public presence/activity projection is the observation path.
gate_descriptions.rex-session-naming: Declared gate: project cwd final directory names the Rex session; identity, role, and task changes do not rename it. Rex endpoint placement is the current block, not tmux position 1.
